overview: This is a "rule," a House resolution that sets the terms for debating other legislation. It sets up votes on two resolutions that would cancel Department of Energy efficiency standards, one for walk-in coolers and freezers and one for commercial refrigerators and freezers, using the Congressional Review Act, a law that lets Congress overturn recent agency rules. Each gets one hour of debate. It also sets up debate on H.R. 1048, which would tighten rules requiring colleges to disclose foreign gifts and contracts and bar contracts with certain foreign entities and countries of concern; only amendments approved by the Rules Committee may be offered to that bill. The House adopted it on March 25, 2025.
for: Supporters say the rule moves measures to a vote efficiently, letting the House act on what they see as costly energy regulations and on concerns about foreign influence at universities.
against: Critics say it limits debate time and amendments on substantive bills, and waives procedural objections that would normally let members raise concerns.
